full_judgment: "Where a case for the reception of secondary evidence is made out under the provisions of section 65, a certified copy of a registered document become admissible in proof of the existence, condition and contents of the original document under the provision of section 57(5) of the Registration Act, but the contents of the documents may not be conclusive evidence. The production of a certified copy of a sale-deed does not, however, warrant the presumption of due execution of the original document. A party producing secondary evidence of a document is not relieved of the duty of proving the execution of the original, Even in a case where a document is exhibited without objection the Court is to be satisfied as to the execution of the document".
